AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND CONTEXT
AbstractText.content: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) is the main cause of low back pain, and nucleus pulposus (NP) cell apoptosis is an important risk factor of IDD. However, the molecular mechanism of this disease remains unknown.

AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: To assess the potential protective effect of CDDO-ethyl amide (EA) against high-glucose-induced oxidative stress injury in NP cells and to investigate the mechanism of antioxidative effects and apoptotic inhibition.

AbstractText.Label: STUDY DESIGN/SETTING
AbstractText.content: To find new molecule to inhibit intervertebral disc degeneration.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Viability, reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and apoptosis were examined in NP cells. The protein expression levels of HO-1 and Nrf2 were measured through Western blot RESULTS: CDDO-EA elicited cytoprotective effects against NP cell apoptosis and ROS accumulation induced by high glucose. CDDO-EA treatment increased the HO-1 and Nrf2 expression abrogated by HO-1, Nrf2, and mitogen-activated protein kinase inhibitors.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: The phosphorylation and nuclear translocation of Nrf2 are crucial for HO-1 overexpression induced by CDDO-EA, which is essential for the cytoprotection against high-glucose-induced oxidative stress in NP cells.
